webpage_capture_policy: For a readable webpage, the default development path is interactive read -> faithful visible-text capture plus source/provenance metadata -> bounded local database capture capsule -> Google Drive handoff. Do not invoke GitHub Actions merely to fetch or archive webpage HTML. The local database is a capture/handoff envelope, not live PostgreSQL authority and not automatic Fact/Judgment publication. Preserve original URL, publisher/source identity, title/date when supported, capture timestamp, capture_mode, visible text, text SHA-256 and any material limitation. Batch many webpages into a bounded task/industry/time capsule when efficient.
github_release_policy: During development, PDFs that require raw source-byte preservation use the existing GitHub Actions acquisition lane: fetch the public PDF, validate/hash it, package it under a unique immutable name, publish it to GitHub Release, then verify the published bytes. Do not use Actions/Release as the default path for readable webpages or HTML merely to preserve page text. Existing historical Release packs that contain HTML/web payloads remain valid immutable legacy assets and may be restored when their old receipts require them; they are not the template for new webpage capture.
google_drive_policy: Google Drive is the development handoff relay for bounded local webpage-capture databases and Longcycle-generated binary state: DuckDB webpage capture capsules, replay materializations, execution/reconciliation outputs, generated database snapshots and offline runtimes. A webpage capture capsule contains source-derived visible text and provenance, so Drive transport does not turn that text into a generated research conclusion or change source authority. Do not put raw PDF source bytes in Drive by default; PDFs use the Actions -> Release lane. Drive is not live transactional database authority.
postgres_policy: Do not transport a live PostgreSQL cluster as session state or place it in GitHub Release. PostgreSQL remains the transactional write/ops engine and is rebuilt in a service-capable runtime when writes, leases or outbox semantics are required. If a generated database snapshot is ever needed for handoff, it belongs in Google Drive and remains a snapshot rather than live authority.
duckdb_policy: DuckDB is the preferred bounded local container for webpage visible-text capture capsules and the portable read/replay materialization for generated research state. During webpage collection it may be written locally in batches; before handoff checkpoint/close it, record SHA-256/size/schema/source count, upload the immutable capsule to Google Drive, and pin the Drive file id plus digest in the repository manifest. After restore, research/replay capsules open read-only by default. Raw PDF source bytes required for re-grounding are restored separately from GitHub Release. Additive older sealed v1 generations remain immutable and are read compatibly; absence of later optional context tables/observation columns is not permission to rewrite historical bytes.
legacy_release_web_policy: Previously produced immutable Release assets that include webpage/HTML bytes are grandfathered. Never mutate or silently relocate them. Restore them only when an existing receipt/current task references them; all new readable webpage captures follow local database -> Google Drive unless a future explicit architecture decision supersedes this policy.
supersession_policy: All handoff transports are immutable-by-identity. Never replace bytes behind a recorded Release filename or Drive file id without advancing the repository manifest and SHA-256. Successor PDF source packs get new Release filenames; successor webpage-capture/generated packs get new Drive files/ids. This manifest is deliberately resume-relevant rather than an exhaustive historical asset inventory; durable receipts retain older artifact identities.
